title: WorkScribe source configuration, version 1
description: One data model for every layer: sources.toml (user), sources.default.toml (fork), policy.toml (organization) and the SourcePolicy dictionary in a configuration profile. TOML, JSON and plist all map onto it. Rules are tried managed → organization → user → fork → built-in, and the first match chooses a chain. Every matching policy entry from every layer applies; prohibitions add up and nothing turns one back off.

user_rules.description: Organization and managed layers only. False: the user's rules are skipped. Their own policy entries still apply.

sources.description: Source instances by id. local-recorder, file-import, notes-only and replay are built in and need no entry unless you configure them.

context_rules.description: Like rules, for context sources (screen, window titles). The built-in default is the screen recorder when screen awareness is on.

capabilities.description: The same object a source sends in its wsp/1 hello. See transcript-source.schema.json#/$defs/capabilities.

kind.description: A built-in kind, or a kind a fork registers in WorkScribeExtensions.

path.description: command: the folder holding source.toml. Relative to this file's folder, absolute, or starting with ~/.

capabilities.description: ingest: required, because there is no manifest. command: taken from source.toml.

watch.description: file-import: a folder to watch for transcripts.

within.description: file-import: only files that appear this soon after the meeting ends.

on_failure.description: Default for rules using this source.

config.description: Passed to the source (wsp/1 hello.config, or the Swift factory). Overrides the manifest's [config].

when.description: All present conditions must match. A list matches any of its values.

app.description: zoom, teams, webex, facetime, slack, discord, meet, browser, or a bundle ID. The app holding the call, not the frontmost app.

window.description: Globs over the call window's title.

name.description: Shown in Settings and in "Why this source?".

use.description: An ordered chain of source ids. notes-only is appended if missing.

on_failure.description: next never moves to a source that captures more than the one that failed.

if_unknown.description: Policy fails closed: an unknown condition counts as matching.

audio.description: forbidden: no source that opens the microphone or captures system audio, and CaptureGate refuses both.

audio_files.description: Transcribing another device's recordings. Defaults to the value of audio.

egress.description: The furthest meeting content may travel from a source.

source_signers.description: Developer ID team IDs a command source's executable must be signed by.
